activity_context.topic_title: Jordan Canonical Decomposition of a 3x3 Matrix

feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}],\,J=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}∗ & 0 & a \\ ∗ & 1 & b \\ ∗ & 2 & c\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices above. Given that $A=PJ{P}^{-1}$ is a Jordan canonical decomposition of $A,$ find the value of $a+c.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since the Jordan block $J$ has a single $3\times 3$ Jordan block corresponding to $\lambda =2,$ the columns of $P$ form the following chain: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3}\overset{A-2I\,}{\to }{v}_{2}\overset{A-2I\,}{\to }{v}_{1}\overset{A-2I\,}{\to }0\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain that 

- the first column of $P$ corresponds to the eigenvector ${v}_{1}$ of the eigenvalue $\lambda =2,$

- the second column of $P$ corresponds to the vector ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ such that $(A-2I){v}_{2}={v}_{1},$

- the third column of $P$ corresponds to the vector ${v}_{3}$ such that $(A-2I){v}_{3}={v}_{2}.$

Now, computing $A-2I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-2I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 2 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the matrix equation $(A-2I){v}_{3}={v}_{2}$ is equivalent to the system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -5 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we have ${x}_{2}=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}-2\cdot 0+{x}_{3}=1\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=1-{x}_{3}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}1-{x}_{3} \\ 0 \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{3}=1,$ we get  

$$
{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a+c=0+1=1.$
